blocks.text: Al-Baseer is a Name found in the Noble Qur'aan in more than 40 places. Examples are,
There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearer, the All-Seer.
Truly, Allah is Ever All-Hearer, All-Seer.

Al-Baseer means the One who sees all visual sights. He sees everything whether minute or small. He sees a crawling black ant on a black rock in the dark night. He sees the path of the morsel of food carried by their limbs. He sees what is beneath the seven earths as He sees what is above the seven heavens. He sees the blinking of the eyelids and the treachery of the eyes. Someone rightly said (some poetry):

O One who sees the beating of the mosquito's wing
In the darkness of the night. The moaning cattle
He sees the place where its veins are suspended in its neck
And its brain from those weakened bones.
Grant me repentance to wipe away from me what I did in my early days.
blocks.ref: Poetry quoted by al-Qurtubi in at-Tathkirah 1/464

blocks.text: Then this magnificent Name instills humility and humbleness. It encourages a person to know that Allaah is observing him and that he should perfect His worship and stay away from disobedience and sins.

Ibn Rajab said, "A man sought to seduce a woman and have his way with her one night. She refused so he said, 'No one can see us except the stars.' She replied 'So where is the One who created the stars?' Meaning, does He not see us. Allaah said,
Knows he not that Allah does see (what he does)?
This was enough of a rebuke and a deterrent."

keyPoints: Al-Baseer is found in the Noble Qur'aan in more than 40 places.
Al-Baseer means the One who sees all visual sights, whether minute or small.
He sees a crawling black ant on a black rock in the dark night, and what is beneath the seven earths just as what is above the seven heavens.
He sees the blinking of the eyelids and the treachery of the eyes.
This Name instills humility and humbleness, and encourages a person to know Allaah is observing him, to perfect his worship and stay away from sins.

evidence.text: There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearer, the All-Seer.
Knows he not that Allah does see (what he does)?

recall.a: The One who sees all visual sights; He sees everything whether minute or small.

recall.q: How many times is Al-Baseer found in the Qur'aan according to the book?
In the story narrated by Ibn Rajab, what did the woman reply when the man said 'No one can see us except the stars'?
recall.a: 'So where is the One who created the stars?' meaning, does He not see us.

recall.q: Which aayah does Ibn Rajab cite after the story of the woman?
recall.a: 'Knows he not that Allah does see (what he does)?' ['Alaq 96:14]

recall.q: What effect does this Name have on the servant?
recall.a: It instills humility and humbleness, and encourages him to know Allaah is observing him, so he perfects his worship and stays away from disobedience and sins.
